tasks.short: Notify supervisors of a major repair.

steps.what: Show the stored equipment record before the repair is discussed.
Notify supervisors when major equipment repairs are needed.

tasks.design: The {OPS_SYSTEM} shows the equipment record already stored for that room. The audio technician tells the supervisor which repair is major. The screen does not write the notice and does not decide that a fault is major. A record with no equipment id is not shown. The conversation is the notification.
tasks.previous_blocker: The fault was described from memory, and the equipment record was a paper tag on the rack.
tasks.enabler_now: The equipment record can be opened before the conversation. The technician still speaks the repair.
tasks.still_hard: Judging that a fault is major enough to stop the show stays with the technician.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor hears the repair from the technician. A stored id is not that conversation.
tasks.altitude: The week still includes the walk to the supervisor. The only change is that the equipment record is open before the conversation starts.

reach.task: Tell a producer that a camera needs repair.
reach.learn: The notice is the conversation, not the asset number.

evidence.claim: Opening an equipment record that is already stored is a lookup. It does not decide that a repair is major.
The notification is the words spoken to the supervisor. Writing those words without the conversation would invent the repair.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: An audio and video technician in a mid-size European company. A stored equipment id is not a repair, and a draft is not the show.

Fields: The equipment id and any fault note already stored. The fault note is not required, because the technician may be the first to see the fault. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the audio technician finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the equipment list already kept for the room before adding a separate register.
unknowns: Whether supervisors expect a written note as well as the conversation.
research_questions: Which faults does this company treat as major enough to stop a show?

already_counted.description: Telling the supervisor about the repair stays with the technician.

incremental.description: Keep the equipment id on the room list after gear is swapped.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The technician still notifies the supervisor in person. Only the opening of an equipment record already on file is removed. A week of faults that are not yet on the record saves the lookup and nothing of the conversation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Show the stored signal path for this media system.
Diagnose and resolve media system problems on the equipment.
Note which media problem was resolved and which remains.

tasks.design: The {OPS_SYSTEM} shows the signal path already drawn for the room. The audio technician diagnoses and resolves the media problem on the equipment. The technician then writes what was resolved. The path drawing does not name the fault. A room with no stored path leaves the screen blank and the technician traces the cables by hand.
tasks.previous_blocker: The signal path lived in a folder, and the resolution was remembered rather than written.
tasks.enabler_now: A stored path can be shown. Finding and fixing the fault is still hands-on.
tasks.still_hard: A path drawing does not reveal a loose connector or a wrong setting in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The technician finds the fault on the equipment and writes what was actually resolved.
tasks.altitude: Diagnosis stays on the equipment. The note records only the resolution the technician has already made, and nothing about the technician is scored.

reach.task: Trace why a screen in the room is not the picture they asked for.
reach.learn: The drawing is not the fault.

evidence.claim: A stored signal path is a diagram of how the room was wired. It is not a diagnosis.
The resolution note is written by the technician after the fix. The equipment id does not supply the words of the note.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: An audio and video technician in a mid-size European company. A stored equipment id is not a repair, and a draft is not the show.
Fields: The room id and the signal path if one is already stored. The path is not invented. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the audio technician finishes it by hand.
Native check: Show the path from the operations list already used for that room before drawing a new one.
The note describes the equipment. It is not a score of the technician.
unknowns: Whether every room already has a signal path worth showing.
research_questions: Who is allowed to change a patch, the technician or the venue?

already_counted.description: Diagnosing the fault and writing the resolution stay with the technician.

incremental.description: Update the signal path when a cable in the room is moved.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The technician still diagnoses and resolves the media problem by hand. Showing a path that is already stored is the only removed time. A room with no path saves nothing, because the screen stays blank.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Show the production call sheet for the assistants.
Direct and coordinate assistants and other personnel during production.
Confirm the production activities the assistants carried out.

tasks.design: The {PROJECT} board shows the call sheet already written for this production. The audio technician directs and coordinates assistants in the room. The technician confirms which activities were carried out. The call sheet does not give the direction. A production with no call sheet leaves the screen blank and the technician directs from the spoken plan.
tasks.previous_blocker: The call sheet was a printout, and changes during the take were shouted and not tied back to it.
tasks.enabler_now: The call sheet can be on screen. Directing the crew during the take cannot leave the room.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing whether an assistant understood the call, while the production is moving, stays with the technician.
tasks.human_edge: The technician directs the people in the room. The call sheet is only the plan they started from.
tasks.altitude: Direction during production stays in the room. The call sheet is visible, and the technician still confirms what the assistants did.

reach.task: Take a call from the floor during a scene.
reach.learn: The call sheet is not the direction given in the moment.

evidence.claim: A call sheet lists who was planned. It does not direct people while the production is underway.
Confirming the activities is the technician's own check. It is not a score of the assistants.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: An audio and video technician in a mid-size European company. A stored equipment id is not a repair, and a draft is not the show.

Fields: The production id and the call sheet if one is already stored. The sheet is not written by this step. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the audio technician finishes it by hand.
Native check: Open the call sheet from the production board already in use before building a new roster.
The confirmation lists activities carried out. It does not rank the assistants.
unknowns: Whether assistants are employees or hired for the day, which changes who may see the sheet.
research_questions: Who changes the call sheet once the production has started?

already_counted.description: Directing the crew and confirming the activities stay with the technician.

incremental.description: Retire call sheets for productions that have closed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Directing assistants during production stays in the room. Only the opening of a call sheet that already exists is removed. A production with no sheet saves nothing of the direction.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compress, duplicate, and store the media.

steps.what: Read the storage location from the job card already filled.
Compress, digitize, and duplicate the audio and video.
Store the copy only after playing the audio and the video.

tasks.design: The {DOCS} store reads the storage location from the job card the technician already filled. The technician compresses, digitizes, and duplicates the audio and video on the equipment, then plays the copy before it is stored. The encoder's run time is not the technician's time and is not counted here. A job card with no location stops the label, and the technician chooses the shelf by hand.
tasks.previous_blocker: The location was written on the tape spine after the copy, and a bad copy was filed anyway.
tasks.enabler_now: The job card can supply the location. The copy and the playback check stay on the equipment.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing a dropout or a clipped soundtrack still takes the technician's ear.
tasks.human_edge: The technician runs the copy and refuses to store it until it has been played.
tasks.altitude: The technician still runs every copy and still plays it back. The location label is read from the job card instead of being typed a second time.

reach.task: File a selected frame only after looking at it.
reach.learn: A location label is not a check of the picture or the sound.

evidence.claim: Reading a storage location from a job card already filled is a field copy. It does not compress the media.
The encoder's running time is the equipment. It is not hours the technician spends, so it is not a labour saving.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: An audio and video technician in a mid-size European company. A stored equipment id is not a repair, and a draft is not the show.

Fields: The job card id and the storage location the technician already entered. The location is not invented. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the audio technician finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the document store the company already files media in before adding a second library.
Encoder run time is outside these shares. The shares are the technician's labelling, the copy work, and the playback.
unknowns: Whether the company already starts encodes from a watch folder with no technician present.
research_questions: Which copies must be played in full before they are stored?

already_counted.description: Running the copy and playing it before storage stay with the technician.

incremental.description: Remove storage locations left behind by cancelled jobs.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The technician still compresses, duplicates, and plays the copy. Only reading a location already written on the job card is removed. Encoder run time was never the technician's hours and is not counted as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The technician still finds the fault, still tells the supervisor, and still runs the copy. A stored equipment id does not become a repair notice, and the encoder's own run is not treated as the technician's time.
reach: Photographers flag a fault on a shoot, and this job learns the notice is what was said to the supervisor.
Actors wait on a call, and this job learns crew direction during the take stays in the room.
skills_to_grow: Say the repair to the supervisor before any notice is written down.
Trace a media fault on the equipment, not from the equipment id alone.
Play a copy before calling it stored.
role.ambitious_version: The technician still decides which fault is major, and a copy is stored only after the technician has heard it play.
